title: कैलाली टीकापुरका मुक्त थारु कमैयाहरुको शिक्षामा पहुँच कम हुनुमा समाजशास्त्रीय अध्ययन {In the Education of freed Tharu Kamaiyas of Kailali Tikapur Sociological Studies on Lack of Access}
authors: ज्ञवाली Gyawali, यज्ञ राज Yagya Raj
nepali: यो शोधपत्र कैलाली टीकापुरका मुक्त थारु कमैयाहरुको शिक्षामा पहु“च कम हुनुको समस्यासंग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । यो अध्ययन त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालय मानविकि संकाय समाजशास्त्र÷मानवशास्त्र विभाग वीरेन्द्रनगर बहुमुखी क्याम्पस अन्तर्गत स्नातकोत्तर तह दोस्रो वर्षको आंशिक उद्देश्य परिपूर्तिका लागि तयार गरिएको छ । यस अध्ययनका उद्देश्यहरु मुक्त थारु कमैयाहरुको शिक्षामा पहु“च कम हुनुका कारणहरु पत्ता लगाउने, मुक्त थारु कमैयाका बालबालिकाहरुको शिक्षा शिक्षा प्रतिको धारणा पहिचान गर्ने र उनीहरुका अभिभावकहरुको शिक्षा प्रतिको धारणा पहिचान गर्ने रहेको  छ । यस अध्ययनको लागि अध्ययन क्ष्ँेत्र छनौट गर्ने क्रममा टीकापुर नगरपालिका अन्तर्गत वडा नं. ७ रानीकुला शिविर वडा नं. ८ विजयनगर शिविर र वडा नं. ९ श्री शक्तिनगर शिवरि छनौट गरिएको थियो । किनभने यो क्षेत्र सदरमुकामवाट करिब ९५ कि.मी. टाढा रहेको छ । साथै यहा“ शैक्षिक स्तर कमजोर रहेकोले पनि यहा“ बसोबास गर्ने मुक्त थारु कमैया जातिहरुको अध्ययन गर्नु आवश्यक भएको हो । यस अध्ययनको लागि सम्बन्धित क्षेत्रका मुक्त थारु कमैयाका बालबालिकाहरु अध्ययन गर्ने ३ वटा सार्वजनिक विद्यालयलाई छनौट गरिएको थियो । यस अध्ययनमा प्राथमिक र द्धितीय स्रोतका तथ्यांकहरुलाई आधार बनाइएको छ । अभिभावक, बालबालिका, प्र.अ., कक्षाध्यापक, जि.शि.का., भूमि सुधार कार्यालय, टीकापुर नगरपालिका र मुक्त कमैयासंग कार्य गर्ने गैर सरकारी संस्थाहरुवाट उद्देश्यमुलक रुपमा प्रश्नावली अन्तरवार्ता सहभागितामुलक अवलोकन र छलफल विधिवाट तथ्यांक संकलन गरिएको थियो । यस अध्ययनवाट मुक्त थारु कमैया बालबालिकाहरुको विद्यालय सहभागिता न्युन रहेको बालबालिकाको विद्यालयमा नियमिततामा कमी रहेको र विद्यालय छोडने दर उच्च रहेको पाइयो । अभिभावकहरुको साक्षारता अवस्था चिन्ताजनक रहेको देखिन्छ । बालबालिकाहरुलाई घरेलु कार्यमा संलग्न हुनु परेको अभिभावकहरु दैनिक ज्यालादारी कामको खोजीका लागि रहनु पर्ने र शिक्षा प्रति उनीहरुको चेतनाको कमी रहेको पनि पाइयो । उक्त समस्याका कारक तत्वहरु बेरोजगारी, गरिबी र अशिक्षा रहेका छन् । उक्त समस्यालाई समाधान गर्न कमैया शिविरमा विद्यालय स्थापना गरि निशुल्क पढाई, कपी, किताब तथा खाजाको समेत व्यवस्था गर्ने सरकारलाई दबाव सिर्जना गर्नुपर्ने, युवा तथा प्रोढका लागि अनौपचारिक शिक्षा कार्यक्रम, सरकारी तथा गैर सरकारी संस्थाको सहयोगमा सञ्चालन गर्नु पर्ने, मुक्त थारु कमैयाहरुलाई तरकारी खेती, पशुपंक्षी पालन, सिलाई कटाई, रेडियो मर्मत र फर्नीचर निर्माण आदि आयमुलक तालिम दिनु पर्ने चेतनामुलक कार्यक्रम (छलफल, पोष्टर, कार्टुन चित्र, सडक नाटक) अदि सञ्चालन गर्नु पर्ने । मुक्त कमैया बालबालिकाहरुलाई औपचारिक शिक्षामा सहभागी गराउन उपयुक्त शैक्षिक निति ल्याउनु पर्ने, निशुल्क सर्वसुलभ र अनिवार्य शैक्षिक कार्यक्रम ल्याउनु पर्ने, उनीहरुको लागि आवास र बसोबासको समस्या समाधान गर्नुपर्ने, बालबालिकाहरुको कक्षा छोड्ने र कक्षा दोहोराउने दर घटाउनु पर्ने मुक्त कमैयाहरुलाई शिक्षाको महत्व बारे जानकारी दिने उनीहरुका बालबालिकाहरुलाई विद्यालयमा समानतापूर्ण व्यवहारको अनुभूति दिनु पर्ने जस्ता समस्याको समाधान गर्न सकेमा शिक्षाको पहु“चमा देखिएको न्युनता वृद्धि गर्न सकिन्छ  भन्ने कुराको सुझावहरु शोध पत्रमा समावेश गरिएको छ ।
american_english:
This research paper relates to the problem of low access to education among the freed Tharu Kamaiyas of Kailali Tikapur.
This study was prepared to partially fulfill the objectives of the second year of the postgraduate level under the Department of Sociology/Anthropology, Faculty of Humanities, Tribhuvan University, Virendranagar Multiple Campus.
The objectives of this study are to find out the causes of low access to education among freed Tharu Kamaiyas, to identify the views on education held by the children of freed Tharu Kamaiyas, and to identify the views on education held by their parents.
While selecting the study area for this study, ward no. 7 Ranikula camp, ward no. 8 Vijaynagar camp and ward no. 9 Shree Shaktinagar camp under Tikapur Municipality were selected.
That is because this area is about 95 km away from the district headquarters.
Also, because the educational level here is weak, it became necessary to study the freed Tharu Kamaiya castes living here.
For this study, three public schools attended by the children of freed Tharu Kamaiyas in the relevant area were selected.
In this study, data from primary and secondary sources were made the basis.
Data was collected purposefully from parents, children, principals, class teachers, the District Education Office, the Land Reform Office, Tikapur Municipality and nongovernmental organizations working with freed Kamaiyas through questionnaires, interviews, participatory observation and discussion.
From this study it was found that the school participation of freed Tharu Kamaiya children is low, that there is a lack of regularity among the children at school, and that the dropout rate is high.
The literacy status of the parents appears alarming.
It was also found that the children have to be involved in household chores, that the parents have to be looking for daily wage work, and that there is a lack of awareness about education among them.
The factors behind the said problem are unemployment, poverty and illiteracy.
To solve the said problem, pressure has to be created on the government to establish schools in the Kamaiya camps and arrange free schooling, notebooks, textbooks and snacks as well, informal education programs for youths and adults have to be run with the support of governmental and nongovernmental organizations, freed Tharu Kamaiyas have to be given income-generating training such as vegetable farming, livestock raising, sewing and tailoring, radio repair and furniture making, and awareness programs (discussions, posters, cartoon drawings, street plays) and so on have to be run.
It is included in the research paper as a suggestion that if problems such as the need to bring a suitable educational policy to involve freed Kamaiya children in formal education, the need to bring a free, universally available and compulsory educational program, the need to solve the housing and residence problem for them, the need to reduce the rate at which children leave class and repeat class, the need to give the freed Kamaiyas information about the importance of education, and the need to give their children a feeling of equal treatment in school can be solved, then the low level seen in access to education can be raised.

informal_english:
This paper's about why freed Tharu Kamaiyas in Kailali Tikapur have such a job getting into education.
It was put together to partly tick off the second-year postgrad requirements under the Department of Sociology/Anthropology, Faculty of Humanities, Tribhuvan University, Virendranagar Multiple Campus.
What we were after was finding out why access to education is low for freed Tharu Kamaiyas, getting a handle on how their kids see education, and doing the same for their mums and dads.
Picking the study area, we went for ward no. 7 Ranikula camp, ward no. 8 Vijaynagar camp and ward no. 9 Shree Shaktinagar camp under Tikapur Municipality.
Reason being, it's about 95 km from the district headquarters.
Plus the education level round here is poor, which is why it was worth having a proper look at the freed Tharu Kamaiya castes living here.
For the study we picked three public schools that the freed Tharu Kamaiya kids go to in the area.
The study leans on data from primary and secondary sources.
We gathered data on purpose from parents, kids, principals, class teachers, the District Education Office, the Land Reform Office, Tikapur Municipality and NGOs working with freed Kamaiyas, using questionnaires, interviews, participatory observation and discussions.
The study found that freed Tharu Kamaiya kids don't take much part in school, that they're not regular, and that the dropout rate is high.
Parents' literacy looks pretty grim.
We also found the kids have to pitch in with housework, the parents have to go looking for daily wage work, and they don't have much awareness about education.
Behind all this sit unemployment, poverty and illiteracy.
To sort it out, pressure needs to go on the government to set up schools in the Kamaiya camps and sort out free schooling, notebooks, textbooks and even snacks, informal education programmes for young people and adults need to be run with help from government and NGOs, freed Tharu Kamaiyas need income-generating training like vegetable farming, livestock keeping, sewing, radio repair and furniture making, and awareness programmes (discussions, posters, cartoon drawings, street plays) and that sort of thing need to be run.
The paper puts in a suggestion that if you can sort out things like bringing in a decent education policy to get freed Kamaiya kids into formal education, bringing in a free, easy-to-reach and compulsory education programme, sorting out their housing and somewhere to live, cutting how often kids leave class and repeat a year, telling freed Kamaiyas why education matters, and giving their kids a sense of fair treatment at school, then that low access to education can be pushed up.
